pages.title: Restaurant Finance Services
pages.heading: Restaurant Finance Services
pages.description: Bring accounting, payroll, bills, reporting and financial guidance into one managed service shaped around your restaurant.
pages.answer: Bring accounting, payroll, bills, reporting and financial guidance into one managed service shaped around your restaurant.

sections.title: Start with the work you need
sections.body: Choose the recurring jobs or financial questions you want help with. We review your systems, records and existing responsibilities before recommending the service.

sections.title: Run, explain and improve
sections.body: Our team handles the defined work, explains the findings and follows up on the next action. The review connects the records to the operating week that produced them.

sections.title: Agree the relationship
sections.body: Your written proposal confirms responsibilities, review dates and fees. Restaurant approvals and specialist work are clearly assigned before the first handoff.

related.label: Find support by the problem you need to solve

pages.title: Restaurant Accounting Services
pages.heading: Restaurant Accounting Services
pages.description: Restaurant accounting that connects sales, bills, payroll and bank activity to a monthly close and a financial review.
pages.answer: Restaurant accounting that connects sales, bills, payroll and bank activity to a monthly close and a financial review.

sections.title: Keep the accounts current
sections.body: We record and reconcile the activity behind your restaurant’s results. Unexplained transactions stay on a review list until the supporting record or answer is available.

sections.title: Read the month with context
sections.body: Your close includes the financial reports we agree to prepare, an explanation of material changes and any questions still outstanding. Reporting dates and incomplete inputs are clearly identified.

sections.title: Agree the approval route
sections.body: Your team confirms operating facts and authorizes payments and filings. Cleanup, tax returns and specialist advice are confirmed separately in your proposal.

related.label: Who handles payroll and bookkeeping together?
Help when restaurant books are behind

pages.title: Restaurant Bookkeeping Services
pages.heading: Restaurant Bookkeeping Services
pages.description: Bring transactions, sales settlements, supplier bills and payroll records into a consistent bookkeeping routine.
pages.answer: Bring transactions, sales settlements, supplier bills and payroll records into a consistent bookkeeping routine.

sections.title: Bring the source records together
sections.body: We work from your accounting records, bank activity, sales statements and invoices. Each recurring input has a delivery date and a contact who can answer questions.

sections.title: Resolve the gaps
sections.body: Missing invoices, unmatched deposits and unclear account entries need follow-up. We investigate the records and keep the unresolved items visible for the close.

sections.title: Prepare for the close
sections.body: Current records give the monthly review a stronger starting point. We agree which close tasks and reports belong in the service, and which remain with your accountant or tax adviser.

related.label: How to compare restaurant bookkeeping services

pages.title: Restaurant Payroll Services
pages.heading: Restaurant Payroll Services
pages.description: Check hours, tip inputs and corrections before payroll cutoff. Keep the records and approvals together through the pay cycle.
pages.answer: Check hours, tip inputs and corrections before payroll cutoff. Keep the records and approvals together through the pay cycle.

sections.title: Check the inputs before cutoff
sections.body: We compare time records, tip inputs and manager corrections for the same pay period. Missing punches and unusual entries go to the person who can confirm what happened.

sections.title: Prepare the approval
sections.body: Your approver receives the prepared records and any questions that remain open. The correction history stays with the source, so a change can be traced later.

sections.title: Confirm processing and tax responsibilities
sections.body: The proposal names who prepares, processes and approves payroll, and who handles payroll-tax work. Your restaurant retains its defined approvals; any specialist advice is identified separately.

related.label: How to compare restaurant payroll services

resources.label: U.S. Department of Labor — Wage and Hour Division

pages.title: Restaurant Tax and Compliance Support
pages.heading: Restaurant Tax and Compliance Support
pages.description: Organize restaurant tax records, deadlines and professional handoffs. Confirm filing and advisory responsibilities before the work begins.
pages.answer: Organize restaurant tax records, deadlines and professional handoffs. Confirm filing and advisory responsibilities before the work begins.

sections.title: Make the records available
sections.body: We organize the accounting, payroll and other records needed for the tax work included in your service. Missing documents and unresolved questions are raised before the agreed handoff.

sections.title: Name who prepares, approves and files
sections.body: Bookkeeping, preparation, filing and tax advice are separate responsibilities. Your proposal states which work Ready Margin handles and which belongs with your CPA or tax adviser.

sections.title: Keep deadlines and notices visible
sections.body: We coordinate the confirmed dates, required records and response contacts. Applicable requirements and professional advice are checked with the relevant authority or qualified adviser.

related.label: Help with restaurant tax and compliance problems

pages.title: Restaurant Compliance Workflow Support
pages.heading: Restaurant Compliance Workflow Support
pages.description: Coordinate confirmed restaurant compliance requirements, source documents and approvals through a documented review process.
pages.answer: Coordinate confirmed restaurant compliance requirements, source documents and approvals through a documented review process.

sections.title: Start with confirmed requirements
sections.body: We work from the obligations confirmed for your business and location. The review records the requirement, its source and the person responsible for completing it.

sections.title: Prepare before the external deadline
sections.body: Internal cutoffs leave time to collect records and obtain approval. Missing information is raised with the relevant contact while there is still time to resolve it.

sections.title: Keep evidence of completion
sections.body: The record includes the approved version and the relevant receipt or confirmation. Filing, interpretation and legal advice are included only when explicitly named in the service.

related.label: Restaurant tax and compliance problem support

resources.label: U.S. Department of Labor — Wage and Hour Division

pages.title: Restaurant CFO Services
pages.heading: Restaurant CFO Services
pages.description: Review cash, costs and performance with a finance partner who connects the reports to your restaurant’s operating decisions.
pages.answer: Review cash, costs and performance with a finance partner who connects the reports to your restaurant’s operating decisions.

sections.title: Start with the decision
sections.body: A staffing change, payment commitment or new location raises different questions. We establish the financial records and assumptions needed for the decision you are making.

sections.title: Understand the financial picture
sections.body: We review performance, cash commitments and cost movements alongside operating context. Forecasts, where included, show their assumptions and the inputs still needing confirmation.

sections.title: Leave with a course of action
sections.body: The review identifies the next checks, responsible people and decisions for your team. Approval, financing and investment authority remain with the restaurant; the service does not guarantee an outcome.

related.label: When does a restaurant need a fractional CFO?

pages.title: Restaurant Financial Consulting
pages.heading: Restaurant Financial Consulting
pages.description: Restaurant financial consulting for owners who need to understand a cost change, cash problem or operating decision.
pages.answer: Restaurant financial consulting for owners who need to understand a cost change, cash problem or operating decision.

sections.title: Define the question
sections.body: Tell us what needs deciding and when. We identify the records required and distinguish confirmed information from estimates.

sections.title: Compare the available options
sections.body: We connect the financial evidence with the restaurant’s trading, staffing and purchasing context. Each option is assessed against the information available and the limits of that information.

sections.title: Agree the next review
sections.body: You receive the findings and a practical sequence of next steps. Recurring support, a specific project or a deeper advisory relationship is priced and confirmed around the work.

pages.title: Restaurant Back-Office Services
pages.heading: Restaurant Back-Office Services
pages.description: Connect bookkeeping, payroll, supplier bills and reporting in one managed restaurant finance service.
pages.answer: Connect bookkeeping, payroll, supplier bills and reporting in one managed restaurant finance service.

sections.title: Choose the jobs we handle
sections.body: We map the recurring work and identify where records or decisions get held up. Your scope names the tasks Ready Margin takes on and the people supplying the inputs.

sections.title: Connect the recurring checks
sections.body: Hours affect payroll. Bills and settlements affect the books. Those records support the financial review. We coordinate the work across the responsibilities included in your service.

sections.title: Keep approvals clear
sections.body: Managers confirm operating facts and nominated people approve payroll, payments and major decisions. Open questions remain visible with the person responsible for resolving them.

pages.title: Restaurant Accounts Payable Services
pages.heading: Restaurant Accounts Payable Services
pages.description: Keep invoices, due dates and review questions together before your restaurant approves a supplier payment.
pages.answer: Keep invoices, due dates and review questions together before your restaurant approves a supplier payment.

sections.title: Record what is due
sections.body: We organize supplier invoices, amounts and payment dates. Delivery questions, missing credits and incomplete documents are recorded with the bill.

sections.title: Check the supporting detail
sections.body: The review compares the available order, delivery and invoice records. A changed pack, quantity or price is investigated before the amount is presented for approval.

sections.title: Prepare the payment review
sections.body: Your approver receives the records and outstanding questions. Payment authority stays with your restaurant, and a reviewed bill is kept distinct from evidence that it was paid.

related.label: Is Ready Margin software or a managed service?
Help with restaurant vendor bill errors

pages.title: Restaurant Cash Flow Management
pages.heading: Restaurant Cash Flow Management
pages.description: Review observed balances, expected receipts and upcoming obligations before the next restaurant payment decision.
pages.answer: Review observed balances, expected receipts and upcoming obligations before the next restaurant payment decision.

sections.title: Begin with a dated balance
sections.body: We establish which accounts and observation dates the cash view covers. Sales and settlement records help explain receipts that have not yet reached the bank.

sections.title: Add the commitments
sections.body: Payroll, supplier bills, rent and other known obligations are placed beside the balance. Confirmed figures, estimates and missing inputs are identified separately.

sections.title: Update before the decision
sections.body: We review timing changes and the questions affecting cash availability. Forecasting is included only with a defined scope and documented assumptions; a projection cannot guarantee future cash.

related.label: How to work through restaurant cash-flow problems

pages.title: Restaurant Food Cost Management
pages.heading: Restaurant Food Cost Management
pages.description: Review supplier prices, purchasing, recipes and stock records to identify the reason behind a food-cost movement.
pages.answer: Review supplier prices, purchasing, recipes and stock records to identify the reason behind a food-cost movement.

sections.title: Make the comparison valid
sections.body: We check the reporting period, units, pack sizes and available stock records before interpreting a change. Missing counts or invoices are identified in the review.

sections.title: Investigate the driver
sections.body: A price increase, portion change, waste issue and count error call for different checks. We trace the movement to the available purchasing and kitchen records.
items: Inventory and waste review where included

sections.title: Discuss the operating response
sections.body: Your team confirms recipes, yields, counts and service conditions. We explain the finding and help prioritize the next check; purchasing and menu decisions stay with your restaurant.

pages.title: Restaurant Labor Cost Management
pages.heading: Restaurant Labor Cost Management
pages.description: Connect schedules, attendance, payroll and sales for a more useful review of restaurant labor costs.
pages.answer: Connect schedules, attendance, payroll and sales for a more useful review of restaurant labor costs.

sections.title: Use the same period
sections.body: We align sales, scheduled hours, recorded time and payroll records. Corrections and incomplete inputs are flagged before comparing one week with another.

sections.title: Explain the movement
sections.body: Lower sales, extra coverage, changed rates and overtime can affect the result in different ways. Manager context helps distinguish an operating change from a record that needs correcting.

sections.title: Make the staffing decision with context
sections.body: We provide the records and analysis for management review. Staffing levels, service requirements, pay policies and employment decisions remain with your restaurant and its appropriate advisers.

pages.title: Restaurant Tip Management Support
pages.heading: Restaurant Tip Management Support
pages.description: Review restaurant tip inputs, unmatched records and corrections through the approved payroll and tip-policy process.
pages.answer: Review restaurant tip inputs, unmatched records and corrections through the approved payroll and tip-policy process.

sections.title: Check the source
sections.body: We review tip records for the relevant period and trace missing names or unusual amounts to the supporting checks. An unresolved amount stays on the review list.

sections.title: Apply the documented process
sections.body: Your restaurant supplies its approved tip policy and the people authorized to interpret or approve it. We organize the inputs and corrections for the work included in your service.

sections.title: Keep the decision with the record
sections.body: The handoff shows what was confirmed, what changed and who approved it. Employment and tax interpretations belong with the relevant qualified adviser unless separately confirmed in scope.

related.label: Help with restaurant tip disputes and discrepancies

pages.title: Restaurant Inventory and Cost Control
pages.heading: Restaurant Inventory and Cost Control
pages.description: Bring restaurant counts, purchases, usage and waste records into a consistent inventory and cost-control review.
pages.answer: Bring restaurant counts, purchases, usage and waste records into a consistent inventory and cost-control review.

sections.title: Check the counting basis
sections.body: We establish the count date, units and location definitions. Transfers, missing items and estimates are recorded so the comparison can be understood.

sections.title: Connect purchases and usage
sections.body: Supplier records, recipes and available waste information help explain movement between counts. Your operating team confirms the quantities and practices behind the records.

sections.title: Improve the next check
sections.body: We identify the process or cost question worth investigating and agree who follows up. The service covers the inventory work named in your proposal; the public workspace preview does not show a dedicated stock-counting tool.

related.label: Help when food cost is too high

pages.title: Restaurant Turnaround Consulting
pages.heading: Restaurant Turnaround Consulting
pages.description: Restaurant turnaround support that starts with cash commitments, current performance and the decisions needing attention first.
pages.eyebrow: Restaurant turnaround / Financial and operating support
pages.answer: Restaurant turnaround support that starts with cash commitments, current performance and the decisions needing attention first.

sections.title: Identify the immediate pressure
sections.body: We review the deadlines, known obligations and decisions that cannot wait. Current cash and operating records establish the starting point, with unknowns clearly marked.

sections.title: Build a sequence the team can carry out
sections.body: We investigate the material cost and performance questions, then agree priorities, responsible people and review dates. A 30/60/90-day plan can be included after the initial diagnosis.

sections.title: Review as the facts change
sections.body: New information may change the order of action. We support the operating review and follow-up; legal, insolvency, lending and investment services require the relevant specialist, and recovery is not guaranteed.

related.label: Help when a restaurant is not profitable

pages.title: Restaurant Profitability Consulting
pages.heading: Restaurant Profitability Consulting
pages.description: Connect restaurant sales, food costs, labor and operating expenses to a focused profitability review.
pages.answer: Connect restaurant sales, food costs, labor and operating expenses to a focused profitability review.

sections.title: Confirm the reporting basis
sections.body: We check the period, account definitions and input completeness before comparing results. A late bill or mismatched payroll period can change what the report appears to say.

sections.title: Find the material changes
sections.body: We separate sales movement, cost movement and timing effects. The supporting records and management’s account of the week help determine which explanation needs checking.

sections.title: Choose a practical next step
sections.body: Your team receives the findings and priorities for review. The next action could be a supplier check, a labor review or a process change; any improvement depends on the decisions and conditions that follow.

related.label: Help when a restaurant is not profitable

pages.title: Multi-Location Restaurant Finance
pages.heading: Multi-Location Restaurant Finance
pages.description: Coordinate restaurant-group records and reporting while retaining the operating detail behind each location’s results.
pages.answer: Coordinate restaurant-group records and reporting while retaining the operating detail behind each location’s results.

sections.title: Set a shared reporting basis
sections.body: We agree account definitions, periods and recurring input dates across the group. Local contacts remain responsible for confirming the facts behind each restaurant’s records.

sections.title: Compare without losing the detail
sections.body: Reports identify missing inputs and differences in format, hours or operating conditions. Consolidation is read alongside the location-level findings.

sections.title: Coordinate the review
sections.body: Group and local decision-makers receive the relevant questions and actions. Entity coverage, consolidation and approval authority are confirmed in your service scope.

pages.title: Outsourced Restaurant Finance Team
pages.heading: Outsourced Restaurant Finance Team
pages.description: An outsourced restaurant finance team for bookkeeping, payroll preparation, payables and reporting. Agree the handoffs and keep your approvals.
pages.answer: An outsourced restaurant finance team for bookkeeping, payroll preparation, payables and reporting. Agree the handoffs and keep your approvals.

sections.title: Give recurring work a named team
sections.body: Choose the jobs you want handled outside your restaurant: bookkeeping, payroll preparation, invoice review or financial reporting. Your scope identifies the Ready Margin contact, the restaurant contact and the records each person supplies.

sections.title: Keep the handoff predictable
sections.body: We agree input dates, review times and the route for urgent questions. Managers confirm operating facts; your nominated approvers retain payroll and payment decisions. Missing information stays visible until it is answered.

sections.title: Review capacity as the work changes
sections.body: A new location, a different pay cycle or a backlog may change the work required. We review the scope and quote with you before adding responsibilities. Specialist tax, legal and payroll processing work is assigned explicitly.
